approach.method_basis: The Parent performs molecular search directly in fixed-width SELFIES token frames. It keeps one real score and the original construction frame for each canonical molecule, ranks observations into a small positive group and lower-scoring negatives, and selects a positive exemplar uniformly. A fresh random coordinate order fixes values from that exemplar until every retained negative frame is excluded, then continues until at most four coordinates remain free. Uniform token draws in the resulting region supply most proposals; a broad uniform component supplies the rest. Molecular validation and novelty filtering precede evaluation, and complete-batch feedback updates the ranked records. Its observed negative exclusions were correct, but the four-coordinate limit determined every final mask, leaving the molecular neighborhoods strongly dependent on each molecule's single retained serialization.
approach.novelty: Add verified equivalent serialization views to the labeled molecular records. Each molecule receives a small, bounded bank of alternative SELFIES frames obtained through graph-preserving atom reorderings and exact molecular identity checks. Each regional classifier selects one view per labeled molecule, so the same real observations can define different token neighborhoods without receiving extra weight. Original sampled frames remain immutable score receipts. This is the lineage's first Child: its only existing implementation always classifies and samples using the one retained original frame. The new causal claim is that changing an equivalent coordinate representation changes decoded regional proposals; a paired diagnostic using the original frames will measure that effect before considering whether scores improve.

hypothesis: For each regional RACOS classifier, uniformly select one identity-verified equivalent SELFIES serialization view per scored molecular record from a bounded task-local view bank, and apply the inherited negative-exclusion, uncertainty-shrinking and uniform-sampling rules to those selected views while preserving one observation weight and the immutable original sampled-frame score receipt per molecule.

finding_summary.headline: Equivalent views changed 782 evaluated proposals; the screening mean fell
finding_summary.insights:
Equivalent construction representatives can change the molecules reached by a local token sampler. The effect comes from different fixed token values: all 1,341 paired regions fixed the same 75 coordinate locations and left four free. Alternative negative views changed when exclusion finished in 652 regions, but never added a final restriction beyond the uncertainty limit. This narrows the demonstrated contribution to the selected exemplar representation under the observed masks. Eleven alternative-view pairs still decoded to the same molecule, so token differences alone would have overstated the effect.

More novel support did not establish better search. Only 36 of 792 accepted children from alternative exemplar views beat their source, compared with 42 of 517 from original views; these conditional groups have different molecule and task support and do not isolate a score effect. The alternatives for generated records also remove an average of 17.58 non-PAD tokens, so this experiment combines atom traversal with normalization of redundant construction tokens. Coverage is uneven: 325 generated records have no admitted alternative, including 137/290 in drd2_docking and 119/290 in sitagliptin_mpo. The paired shadows have no scores, leaving both the contribution to later optimization and reliability across seeds open.

The supplied molecular assessment still finds frequent radicals, unusual charges and reactive or strained connectivity among generated molecules, including high scorers. Exact identity verification protects the already scored bank entries; it does not make their sampled offspring chemically credible or preserve useful scaffold relationships. Useful, chemically ordinary molecular neighborhoods remain unresolved despite the demonstrated representation effect.
finding_summary.results:
The equivalent views produced a measurable molecular effect. Verified alternatives were available for 1,175 of 1,500 scored records, and an alternative exemplar was selected in 808 of 1,341 regional constructions. Holding the molecular observations and sampling randomness fixed, 797 paired proposals decoded to different molecules; 782 of those changes survived filtering and received real evaluator scores. All identity, one-observation, score-attachment and batch checks passed.

Regional novelty acceptance rose from 96.24% to 97.61%, and decoded overlaps across regions fell from 48 of 1,355 raw draws to 31 of 1,341. The fraction of accepted regional children beating their exemplar rose slightly, from 67/1,304 (5.14%) to 78/1,309 (5.96%). The five-task final Top-1 mean nevertheless fell from 0.315539 to 0.289335. Parent-to-current maxima were 0.345581 to 0.366339 for zaleplon_mpo, 0.579123 to 0.571504 for deco_hop, 0.120104 to 0.028849 for drd2_docking, 0.167839 to 0.168550 for median_2, and 0.365051 to 0.311434 for sitagliptin_mpo. Both runs completed all five tasks with 300 evaluations each. This is one screening seed.

molecular.headline: Frequent rings conceal radical-rich chemistry: recognizable aryl/carbonyl scaffolds coexist with highly charged polyenes and strained rings.
molecular.overall_character: The digest and all supplied current and Parent seed-0 trajectories were read. Each covered task contains 300 observations, including 290 optimizer proposals; no tasks lack trajectories. The output ranges from tiny fragments to medium and larger multiring frameworks. Ring_closure_rate spans 0.6966 to 0.8172, but aromatic_atom_rate spans 0.0207 to 0.6: ring construction is common while intact aromatic chemistry is very uneven. These digest rates measure the presence of SMILES text features in proposed molecules, not fractions of atoms or perceived ring counts. The recognizable families include haloaryl indole carboxamides, methoxy chromenone/pyridyl assemblies, and aryl ester/dicarbonyl frameworks. Other high-scoring families are almost entirely nonaromatic polyenes, cumulenes and unusual heteroatom rings. Charged_rate spans 0.6897 to 0.9448. Read-only RDKit reparsing of the supplied graphs confirms frequent radical centres, including in leading molecules and in some structures without formal charge. Low-coordinate boron, carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus and silicon environments coexist with oxonium, unusual sulfur bonding, peroxide-like chains and strained unsaturation. Synthetic plausibility is poor overall; neutral carbonyl-rich examples and some conventional aromatic fragments provide a more credible subset. Formal graph diversity is substantial, but stronger proposals within a task repeatedly revisit related families, giving moderate useful structural diversity. Every proposal set has stereocentre_rate 0.0, establishing absent stereochemical specification rather than absence of potentially stereogenic atoms. Parent comparisons below describe observed chemistry and supplied scores; neither those comparisons nor local score associations identify an unseen target pharmacophore or establish a causal score contribution from a particular chemical feature.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly medium-sized, branched, unsaturated frameworks with haloaryl carboxamides, alongside small fragments. Mean SMILES length is 42.9 and maximum length 84; ring_closure_rate is 0.8172, aromatic_atom_rate 0.5655 and halogen_rate 0.7552. Evaluation 30 retains a methoxyindole carboxamide linked to fluorophenyl, but carries a radical-bearing boron anion. Evaluation 268 instead combines a bromophenyl aminoacetamide with an unsaturated oxygen-containing bicyclic core and low-coordinate boron/nitrogen substituents. The intact amide and aromatic fragments are recognizable synthetic chemistry; the electronic states and reorganized unsaturated rings make the leading complete structures implausible ordinary synthetic targets. Charged_rate is 0.831.
liabilities: Low-coordinate boron anions and additional radical nitrogen/phosphorus centres. Evaluation 189 has compensating formal charges while retaining radical centres, so net neutrality does not establish credible electronic structure.
Extensively rearranged unsaturated rings, atypical sulfur substitution and unspecified stereochemistry make scaffold geometry and synthesis uncertain.
missing_features: Reliable coverage of chemically ordinary variants retaining the haloaryl-carbonyl/nitrogen architecture visible in the stronger molecules. The supplied neutral indole carboxamide shows a credible version, but the leading generated variants add radical-bearing atoms.

Controlled variation of intact heteroaromatic and amide arrangements beyond repeated ring expansion and heteroatom insertion. The equal scores of the aromatic and partly nonaromatic relatives prevent inferring a universal requirement for additional aromatic rings.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial neutral methoxyindole carboxamide at evaluation 9 scores 0.3051048083696145; the boron-anion indole at evaluation 30 scores 0.354481213984869, and its ring-expanded, partly nonaromatic relative at evaluation 174 has exactly the same score. The aminoacetamide/bromophenyl framework at evaluation 268 reaches 0.36633919598396925. Thus the visible upper tail preserves assembled aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl relationships, while strict aromaticity alone does not explain the score. The tiny epoxide at evaluation 298 scores 0.0; the final sulfur-containing ring-reorganized aminoacetamide at evaluation 300 scores 0.2966478915460209. Parent n-e8acbddfa050 reached 0.3455806835841063 with a nitrogen/thione-rich multiring framework carrying oxonium and low-coordinate charged atoms. The current upper tail shifts toward haloaryl carboxamides and boron-bearing unsaturated cores, while unusual electronic states persist.

per_task.generated_character: The stronger molecules are medium-to-large aromatic assemblies containing methoxy-substituted chromenone-like carbonyl heterocycles, phenyl/pyridyl regions and often nitriles. Mean SMILES length is 46.9 and maximum length 86; ring_closure_rate is 0.7793 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.5828. Hydrazinium substituents recur. Evaluation 237 incorporates an extended unsaturated ring bridge, imidate-like connectivity and an O-N substituent. Evaluation 199 combines a reorganized lactone/oxonium ring system with a charged O-O-O chain. The aromatic and carbonyl components are recognizable, but the elaborate cyclizations and reactive decorations make the overall synthetic plausibility questionable to poor. Charged_rate is 0.8276.
liabilities: Peroxide-like O-O chains, multiply charged oxygen environments and the O-Br bond in the final small acyl hypobromite at evaluation 299.

Ring-contracted lactone connectivity, extended unsaturated bridges and recurrent N-N/N-O functionality require specific stability and synthetic justification. The leading evaluation 237 is closed-shell on reparsing, but that does not establish an accessible synthetic route.
missing_features: Broader stable decoration chemistry around the aromatic/polar frameworks. The current upper tail repeatedly uses hydrazinium, aminooxy or oxonium/oxygen-chain functionality, while the Parent contained a relatively strong neutral aryl-aminal example.

Coherent alternatives that retain useful aryl/carbonyl relationships without requiring highly rearranged lactone rings or long unsaturated cyclization bridges. Exact hidden decoration requirements cannot be inferred from these trajectories.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial methoxy chromenone/biaryl nitrile at evaluation 8 scores 0.5418375031378128; the pyridyl-nitrile/hydrazinium derivative at evaluation 37 scores 0.5643691820162409. The oxonium/methylthio-containing evaluation 249 receives the same 0.5643691820162409, despite its additional oxonium centre and altered substituents. The ring-bridged evaluation 237 scores 0.5715043852298755 and the charged oxygen-chain relative at evaluation 199 scores 0.5684258279147134. Acetylene at evaluation 246 scores 0.5. The final extensively rearranged, nonaromatic polycycle at evaluation 300 scores 0.507630410654828. The observed preference is for assembled aromatic/polar architectures over tiny or strongly disrupted structures; the score does not show that reactive oxygen or hydrazine functionality is necessary. The Parent upper tail instead emphasized indole amidine/carboxamide and diaryl cyclic-aminal families: its maximum was 0.5791225581141548 and a neutral diaryl hydroxyaminal scored 0.5766980825479363. The current maximum is associated with a different, still chemically problematic aromatic family.

per_task.generated_character: The upper tail consists of relatively large nonaromatic polyenes/cumulenes, branched chains and large unsaturated rings. Mean SMILES length is 60.7 and maximum length 109. Ring_closure_rate is 0.6966, but aromatic_atom_rate is only 0.0207; charged_rate is 0.9448 and cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.6207. The best molecule, evaluation 277, is acyclic. Evaluation 293 closes a long heteroatom-bearing unsaturated chain into a large ring. Both contain repeated carbon cations, boron anions, low-coordinate phosphorus, unusual sulfur multiple bonds and oxonium environments. Reparsing confirms multiple radical centres in these leading graphs. They express extensive formal unsaturation and heteroatom diversity with very little conventional medicinal scaffold chemistry, making them implausible ordinary isolable compounds.
liabilities: Numerous radical centres and low-coordinate charged atoms, including repeated carbon cations, boron anions and atypical sulfur/phosphorus multiple bonds within individual molecules.

Long cumulated/conjugated sequences and highly unsaturated macrocyclic or bridged connectivity with unspecified geometry. A ring-closure digit here supplies little evidence for a stable, useful three-dimensional scaffold.
missing_features: Chemically credible closed-shell realizations of the larger carbon frameworks and polar functionality represented in the current upper tail. Its apparent size/architecture preference is realized through highly unusual electronic states.

Coverage of intact aryl-containing, constrained polar architectures is greatly reduced relative to the Parent upper tail. The low-scoring aromatic and tertiary-amine examples show that neither adding a generic aromatic ring nor adding an amine is an evidence-backed solution by itself.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The long acyclic evaluation 277 scores 0.028848761971118526 and the large-ring relative at evaluation 293 scores 0.02884865939301175. The similarly elaborate final evaluation 296 scores 0.02884463593273818. A much shorter boron/nitrogen/oxygen ionic fragment at evaluation 212 scores 0.0020518739328129186; the final short brominated oxonium ether at evaluation 295 scores 0.004062928989281451. Within this trajectory, fuller nonaromatic carbon/heteroatom frameworks generally occupy the upper tail, with little separation among the largest relatives. Simple aromatic presence is insufficient: the biphenyl nitrile/alkoxide at evaluation 16 scores 0.0013501216598358666, and the initial aromatic amide/hydroxamate with a saturated tertiary amine at evaluation 6 scores 0.0003786988088202195. The Parent maximum, 0.12010438063540518, came from a halogenated aryl-containing polycycle with its own unusual sulfur/nitrogen chemistry. The current maximum accompanies near-loss of aromatic frameworks and growth of nonaromatic chains/large rings; this comparison does not isolate why the scores differ.

per_task.generated_character: The stronger molecules are medium-to-large aryl ethyl-ester/dicarbonyl frameworks with N-methyl carbonyl or urea-like regions, phenol/ether substituents and substantial ring rearrangement. Mean SMILES length is 48.7 and maximum length 84; ring_closure_rate is 0.8034 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.6. Evaluation 243 is a neutral aryl-ester macrocycle joining the carbonyl/nitrogen region through an N-O-methylene-O linkage. Evaluations 282 and 298 are also neutral and closed-shell, retaining aryl and dicarbonyl motifs in cross-conjugated or ring-expanded arrangements. These are more recognizable synthetic targets than much of the remaining output, although their cyclizations and reactive linkages remain demanding. Charged_rate is 0.6897; uncharged phosphorus-containing relatives also carry radicals on reparsing.
liabilities: N-O/acetal-like linkage in the leading macrocycle and extensive cross-conjugation or ring expansion in nearby neutral structures; chemical stability and synthetic accessibility are unestablished.

Phosphorus/silicon insertions, radicals and charged replacements elsewhere in the same families. Evaluation 53 lacks formal charge but contains a radical-bearing phosphorus environment, illustrating an electronic-state problem that charge counting alone misses.
missing_features: More controlled, stable variations of the aromatic/ester/carbonyl arrangement supported by the stronger molecules. Current high-scoring neutral examples exist, but often reach new topology through extended cyclization or N-O connectivity.

Broader development of distinct intact aromatic amide-rich families, exemplified by the relatively strong initial amide/hydroxamate, alongside the dominant ester/dicarbonyl family. The observations do not reveal an unseen reference structure.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl ester/fused dicarbonyl at evaluation 7 scores 0.1678386594791329. The generated macrocycle at evaluation 243 scores 0.16854996561581048; evaluations 282 and 298 score 0.16695175953014704 and 0.1651413292730383. Adding the sulfur-oxygen substituent in the related evaluation 271 gives 0.160745220268056. The late short brominated ether at evaluation 299 scores 0.020160580116942894, while the small imidate-like anion at evaluation 292 scores 0.0. The gradient supports retention of assembled aromatic/ester/carbonyl relationships over fragments; substantial rearrangements within that family remain close in score. The chemically distinct initial aromatic amide/hydroxamate at evaluation 6 also scores 0.1569767171139282. The Parent retained the same initial maximum of 0.1678386594791329, with its best generated annulated dicarbonyl relative at 0.16526725762745997. The current leading chemistry remains centered on the same ester/dicarbonyl family while exploring new neutral ring topologies.

per_task.generated_character: The stronger output comprises medium-sized, mostly nonaromatic fluorinated amino/polyene frameworks, unusual boron/phosphorus rings, and imine-containing polycycles with silicon or selenium. Mean SMILES length is 44.4 and maximum length 84; ring_closure_rate is 0.7828, aromatic_atom_rate 0.2138, charged_rate 0.9241 and cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.4483. Evaluation 298 links an amino-substituted unsaturated ring to a methoxy-substituted small cyclic alkyne bearing adjacent carbon anions, and adds a boron/sulfur/iodine appendage. Evaluation 210 combines fluorophosphorus and boron/oxygen ring chemistry with carbon anions; evaluation 223 is a long acyclic unsaturated nitrogen/oxygen/sulfur chain. These upper-tail structures contain radicals and unusual ionic states. The cyclic alkyne geometry and heteroatom connectivity make their synthetic plausibility especially poor.
liabilities: Adjacent radical-bearing carbon anions, nitrogen anions, unusual boron/sulfur/iodine connectivity and low-coordinate phosphorus, silicon or selenium environments in stronger molecules.
A highly strained small cyclic alkyne in the leading family, extended cumulenes/polyenes in other strong members, and absent stereochemical specification.
missing_features: Stable closed-shell versions of the medium-sized fluorinated, nitrogen-bearing chain/ring architectures represented in the upper tail, with controlled ionization and feasible bond geometry.

Chemically ordinary amine/ether and related polar substitutions that can vary those architectures without carbon-anion/radical arrays, cyclic alkynes or low-coordinate heteroatoms. Their score effect remains unmeasured; the data do not justify prescribing a missing aromatic pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Evaluation 298 scores 0.31143387897841074. Its hydroxyl-bearing relative at evaluation 187 scores 0.25352114095863515: replacing that oxygen substituent with the nitrogen-anion environment changes the score locally, while introducing additional electronic-state concerns. The distinct ring-containing evaluation 210 scores 0.30182012887455895; the acyclic evaluation 223 scores 0.28798101896372785 and its cyclized relative at evaluation 109 scores 0.26731656125719533. Rings and aromaticity therefore cannot be treated as universal requirements for the visible high-score region. The related final cyclic-alkyne framework at evaluation 296 scores only 3.830424901142501e-06, and the heteroatom-dense charged chain at evaluation 20 scores 4.0773933311719747e-53. The observed median is 6.8e-05. The score is sensitive to the particular assembled carbon/heteroatom arrangement; size and charge density alone do not explain it. The Parent maximum was 0.36505100258606615 in another radical-rich fluorinated unsaturated nitrogen/oxygen/phosphorus family. The current upper tail uses different ring and amino motifs without establishing more credible chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The supplied proposal sets have charged_rate from 0.6897 to 0.9448. Reparsing the trajectory graphs confirms radical centres in leading boron-substituted aryl carboxamides, carbon-anion amino frameworks and phosphorus/sulfur polyenes. Some formally uncharged phosphorus-containing dicarbonyl relatives also contain radicals. Neutral closed-shell aryl/carbonyl examples are present in strong score regions, demonstrating useful conventional electronic-state coverage that is inconsistently maintained.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve chemically credible electronic states when varying polar and ionizable functionality.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make closed-shell polar structures and chemically ordinary ionization states routinely accessible through joint control of bond patterns, valence, radical state and protonation. Account for compensating charges and neutral radicals as well as net charge. Let observed feedback determine which polar arrangements matter.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Leading digest molecules include small cyclic alkynes, charged oxygen chains, reorganized lactone rings and long cumulene-rich loops. A stronger neutral macrocycle retains an N-O-methylene-O linkage, while a methoxy-bearing aromatic molecule and its oxonium/methylthio variant have identical scores. Frequent ring closures therefore coexist with chemically strained or reactive architectures, and their presence does not show that those liabilities are needed for the score.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks consistent functional-group stability and feasible ring geometry even when a graph parses successfully.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide stable, ordinary substitution and ring-construction options that maintain complete functional groups and feasible unsaturation. Represent ring strain and labile bond combinations alongside local valence so that changing a substituent need not create a cyclic alkyne, peroxide chain or unsupported heteroatom multiple bond.

transferable_gaps.evidence: High-scoring excerpts repeatedly retain assembled aryl/carboxamide or aryl/ester/dicarbonyl motifs, whereas low-score and final excerpts include tiny fragments or substantially disrupted variants. One current trajectory has aromatic_atom_rate 0.0207 despite ring_closure_rate 0.6966; its upper tail consists of nonaromatic chains and large loops, while the Parent upper tail retained aryl polycycles. A different high-score family includes strong acyclic members, showing that the gap concerns coherent arrangements supported by feedback rather than ring presence alone.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator inconsistently preserves useful scaffold and linker relationships while exploring new molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support coherent substitution and attachment changes that preserve the ring edges and complete linker/functional-group patterns of useful observed structures. Keep distinct intact scaffold families accessible, with preservation and diversification guided by current molecular feedback.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every proposal set has stereocentre_rate 0.0. Stronger ring-containing examples are dominated by unsaturated, ring-expanded or unusually charged architectures. Ordinary saturated nitrogen rings occur in the supplied initial chemistry, but the leading generated structures often express nitrogen functionality through hydrazinium, imines, radical anions or heteroatom-rich unsaturated loops. This identifies a coverage gap; the visible scores do not establish a universal benefit from saturation, a basic amine or stereochemical specification.
transferable_gaps.gap: Conventional saturated heterocycle and stereochemically specified structure coverage is weak among the stronger generated molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make feasible saturated and partly saturated heterocycles, controlled amine ionization and explicitly specified stereochemical alternatives available as general construction choices. Preserve their bond geometry and identity through variation, and use task-local feedback to determine where that chemistry is useful.

method_name: RACOS: negative-exclusion sampling of de novo SELFIES regions
method_thesis: The anchor is RACOS, selected before locating the primary source. Its categorical form chooses a positively labeled exemplar, randomly fixes coordinates to that exemplar until negative examples are excluded, further restricts the number of free coordinates, and samples the resulting region; a broader uniform component preserves exploration. Each proposal can use a newly randomized classifier. These are the mechanisms described by Yu, Qian and Hu in [Derivative-Free Optimization via Classification](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/10289/10148). My molecular adaptation applies this process directly to bounded categorical SELFIES frames, with removable padding that permits changes in molecular length. Preparation extracts only a construction-token alphabet from the permitted unlabeled corpus. There is no trained molecular encoder or decoder. Initial labeled molecules become exemplars only after encoding and decoding reproduce their canonical identity. For generated molecules, retain the actual sampled frame, its decoded canonical molecule, and the score actually returned for that molecule. Rank the current objective's observed molecules into a high-score positive group and a lower-score negative group; use these labels to construct exclusion regions. Free token positions are newly sampled and decoded into complete molecules, checked, canonicalized, and deduplicated. Rebuild a region or use the broad generation component when a region cannot provide a fresh molecule. These are online constructions from token primitives, not retrieval or enumeration of complete molecules. After each announced batch receives real feedback, refresh the labeled sets and incumbent; all pending proposals use only previously observed scores. Each objective starts with clean task-specific state and follows the protocol's supplied batch and resource limits. The hypothesis is that explicitly excluding observed poor token configurations will concentrate new molecular proposals around combinations that improve the incumbent with few labels. Success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Region exclusion, validity, or classification accuracy alone cannot establish that hypothesis. Positional token restrictions may have weak structural meaning, and multiple frames can decode to the same molecule; exact representation checks address score provenance but do not establish useful search geometry.

approach.method_basis: The Parent performs molecular search directly in fixed-width SELFIES token frames. It keeps one real score and the original construction frame for each canonical molecule, ranks observations into a small positive group and lower-scoring negatives, and selects a positive exemplar uniformly. A fresh random coordinate order fixes values from that exemplar until every retained negative frame is excluded, then continues until at most four coordinates remain free. Uniform token draws in the resulting region supply most proposals; a broad uniform component supplies the rest. Molecular validation and novelty filtering precede evaluation, and complete-batch feedback updates the ranked records. Its observed negative exclusions were correct, but the four-coordinate limit determined every final mask, leaving the molecular neighborhoods strongly dependent on each molecule's single retained serialization.
approach.novelty: Add verified equivalent serialization views to the labeled molecular records. Each molecule receives a small, bounded bank of alternative SELFIES frames obtained through graph-preserving atom reorderings and exact molecular identity checks. Each regional classifier selects one view per labeled molecule, so the same real observations can define different token neighborhoods without receiving extra weight. Original sampled frames remain immutable score receipts. This is the lineage's first Child: its only existing implementation always classifies and samples using the one retained original frame. finding_summary.headline: Equivalent views changed 782 evaluated proposals; the screening mean fell
finding_summary.insights:
Equivalent construction representatives can change the molecules reached by a local token sampler. The effect comes from different fixed token values: all 1,341 paired regions fixed the same 75 coordinate locations and left four free. Alternative negative views changed when exclusion finished in 652 regions, but never added a final restriction beyond the uncertainty limit. This narrows the demonstrated contribution to the selected exemplar representation under the observed masks. Eleven alternative-view pairs still decoded to the same molecule, so token differences alone would have overstated the effect.

More novel support did not establish better search. Only 36 of 792 accepted children from alternative exemplar views beat their source, compared with 42 of 517 from original views; these conditional groups have different molecule and task support and do not isolate a score effect. The alternatives for generated records also remove an average of 17.58 non-PAD tokens, so this experiment combines atom traversal with normalization of redundant construction tokens. Coverage is uneven: 325 generated records have no admitted alternative, including 137/290 in drd2_docking and 119/290 in sitagliptin_mpo. The paired shadows have no scores, leaving both the contribution to later optimization and reliability across seeds open.

The supplied molecular assessment still finds frequent radicals, unusual charges and reactive or strained connectivity among generated molecules, including high scorers. Exact identity verification protects the already scored bank entries; it does not make their sampled offspring chemically credible or preserve useful scaffold relationships. Useful, chemically ordinary molecular neighborhoods remain unresolved despite the demonstrated representation effect.
finding_summary.results:
The equivalent views produced a measurable molecular effect. Verified alternatives were available for 1,175 of 1,500 scored records, and an alternative exemplar was selected in 808 of 1,341 regional constructions. Holding the molecular observations and sampling randomness fixed, 797 paired proposals decoded to different molecules; 782 of those changes survived filtering and received real evaluator scores. All identity, one-observation, score-attachment and batch checks passed.

Regional novelty acceptance rose from 96.24% to 97.61%, and decoded overlaps across regions fell from 48 of 1,355 raw draws to 31 of 1,341. The fraction of accepted regional children beating their exemplar rose slightly, from 67/1,304 (5.14%) to 78/1,309 (5.96%). The five-task final Top-1 mean nevertheless fell from 0.315539 to 0.289335. Parent-to-current maxima were 0.345581 to 0.366339 for zaleplon_mpo, 0.579123 to 0.571504 for deco_hop, 0.120104 to 0.028849 for drd2_docking, 0.167839 to 0.168550 for median_2, and 0.365051 to 0.311434 for sitagliptin_mpo. finding_summary.insights:
Equivalent construction representatives can change the molecules reached by a local token sampler. The effect comes from different fixed token values: all 1,341 paired regions fixed the same 75 coordinate locations and left four free. Alternative negative views changed when exclusion finished in 652 regions, but never added a final restriction beyond the uncertainty limit. This narrows the demonstrated contribution to the selected exemplar representation under the observed masks. Eleven alternative-view pairs still decoded to the same molecule, so token differences alone would have overstated the effect.

More novel support did not establish better search. Only 36 of 792 accepted children from alternative exemplar views beat their source, compared with 42 of 517 from original views; these conditional groups have different molecule and task support and do not isolate a score effect. The alternatives for generated records also remove an average of 17.58 non-PAD tokens, so this experiment combines atom traversal with normalization of redundant construction tokens. Coverage is uneven: 325 generated records have no admitted alternative, including 137/290 in drd2_docking and 119/290 in sitagliptin_mpo. The paired shadows have no scores, leaving both the contribution to later optimization and reliability across seeds open.

The supplied molecular assessment still finds frequent radicals, unusual charges and reactive or strained connectivity among generated molecules, including high scorers. Exact identity verification protects the already scored bank entries; it does not make their sampled offspring chemically credible or preserve useful scaffold relationships. Useful, chemically ordinary molecular neighborhoods remain unresolved despite the demonstrated representation effect.

finding_summary.insights:
Equivalent construction representatives can change the molecules reached by a local token sampler. The effect comes from different fixed token values: all 1,341 paired regions fixed the same 75 coordinate locations and left four free. Alternative negative views changed when exclusion finished in 652 regions, but never added a final restriction beyond the uncertainty limit. This narrows the demonstrated contribution to the selected exemplar representation under the observed masks. Eleven alternative-view pairs still decoded to the same molecule, so token differences alone would have overstated the effect.

More novel support did not establish better search. Only 36 of 792 accepted children from alternative exemplar views beat their source, compared with 42 of 517 from original views; these conditional groups have different molecule and task support and do not isolate a score effect. The alternatives for generated records also remove an average of 17.58 non-PAD tokens, so this experiment combines atom traversal with normalization of redundant construction tokens. Coverage is uneven: 325 generated records have no admitted alternative, including 137/290 in drd2_docking and 119/290 in sitagliptin_mpo. The paired shadows have no scores, leaving both the contribution to later optimization and reliability across seeds open.

The supplied molecular assessment still finds frequent radicals, unusual charges and reactive or strained connectivity among generated molecules, including high scorers. Exact identity verification protects the already scored bank entries; it does not make their sampled offspring chemically credible or preserve useful scaffold relationships. Useful, chemically ordinary molecular neighborhoods remain unresolved despite the demonstrated representation effect.

Low-coordinate boron, carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus and silicon environments coexist with oxonium, unusual sulfur bonding, peroxide-like chains and strained unsaturation. transferable_gaps.evidence: The supplied proposal sets have charged_rate from 0.6897 to 0.9448. Reparsing the trajectory graphs confirms radical centres in leading boron-substituted aryl carboxamides, carbon-anion amino frameworks and phosphorus/sulfur polyenes. Some formally uncharged phosphorus-containing dicarbonyl relatives also contain radicals. Neutral closed-shell aryl/carbonyl examples are present in strong score regions, demonstrating useful conventional electronic-state coverage that is inconsistently maintained.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve chemically credible electronic states when varying polar and ionizable functionality.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make closed-shell polar structures and chemically ordinary ionization states routinely accessible through joint control of bond patterns, valence, radical state and protonation. Account for compensating charges and neutral radicals as well as net charge. Let observed feedback determine which polar arrangements matter.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Leading digest molecules include small cyclic alkynes, charged oxygen chains, reorganized lactone rings and long cumulene-rich loops. A stronger neutral macrocycle retains an N-O-methylene-O linkage, while a methoxy-bearing aromatic molecule and its oxonium/methylthio variant have identical scores. Frequent ring closures therefore coexist with chemically strained or reactive architectures, and their presence does not show that those liabilities are needed for the score.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks consistent functional-group stability and feasible ring geometry even when a graph parses successfully.

applicability_conditions: Applies when a scored molecule admits alternative non-PAD SELFIES token sequences whose complete decoded canonical/isomeric identity is exact within the already frozen alphabet and width. Uniform view choice is over the finite verified bank and uniform token sampling is over the selected raw categorical region. Neither distribution is uniform over molecular identities or over all equivalent serializations.

Equivalent serialization can normalize redundant construction tokens as well as change atom traversal. The intervention tests the combined choice of an equivalent construction representative; it does not isolate atom traversal from all other identity-preserving encoding changes.

Molecular scores and labels belong to the single original record. Verification permits an equivalent frame to represent that record during classification; it supplies neither another observation nor a score for any changed molecule.

Same-state paired decodes isolate immediate proposal effects without obtaining counterfactual scores or controlling the later feedback trajectory. View diversity or molecular divergence does not establish improved chemical plausibility, calibrated local smoothness or a repeatable Top-1 advantage.

approach.method_basis: The Parent performs molecular search directly in fixed-width SELFIES token frames. It keeps one real score and the original construction frame for each canonical molecule, ranks observations into a small positive group and lower-scoring negatives, and selects a positive exemplar uniformly. A fresh random coordinate order fixes values from that exemplar until every retained negative frame is excluded, then continues until at most four coordinates remain free. Uniform token draws in the resulting region supply most proposals; a broad uniform component supplies the rest. Molecular validation and novelty filtering precede evaluation, and complete-batch feedback updates the ranked records. Its observed negative exclusions were correct, but the four-coordinate limit determined every final mask, leaving the molecular neighborhoods strongly dependent on each molecule's single retained serialization.
approach.novelty: Add verified equivalent serialization views to the labeled molecular records. Each molecule receives a small, bounded bank of alternative SELFIES frames obtained through graph-preserving atom reorderings and exact molecular identity checks. Each regional classifier selects one view per labeled molecule, so the same real observations can define different token neighborhoods without receiving extra weight. Original sampled frames remain immutable score receipts. This is the lineage's first Child: its only existing implementation always classifies and samples using the one retained original frame. The new causal claim is that changing an equivalent coordinate representation changes decoded regional proposals; a paired diagnostic using the original frames will measure that effect before considering whether scores improve.

research_intent.falsifier: Equivalent-view activation is refuted if usable nonoriginal banks exist but regional construction never selects them, or the sampler still starts from the immutable original frame after a nonoriginal exemplar view was selected. The molecular-neighborhood claim is not demonstrated if every valid paired actual/counterfactual decode has the same canonical identity; token changes alone are insufficient. Require changed-view use and at least one paired canonical proposal change that reaches an actual emitted region, while reporting all counts rather than presenting a single event as broad coverage. If bounded encoding yields no usable alternatives, the applicability prerequisite failed and the view contribution is inconclusive. Any admitted view that changes canonical/isomeric identity, alters category meanings or width, duplicates a record's observation weight, changes an original sampled receipt, attaches a score without its existing identity check, or uses unresolved feedback violates the bound mechanism. Incorrect active-view exclusion, free-coordinate sampling, mixture or batch size also violates the implementation. A shadow decode consuming live RNG or modifying search state invalidates its causal comparison. Missing receipts make activation inconclusive. Lower score, continued alias overlap, unchanged negative final-mask contribution or absent chemical plausibility gains alone do not refute correctly executed equivalent-view sampling.
